pharm: Urinary antispasmodic / anticholinergic for overactive bladder
quick: 20 mg orally twice daily, at least 1 hour before meals or on an empty stomach
Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before a meal, with water (food reduces absorption)
Use only if clearly needed; limited human data (former Category C)
Avoid or use with caution; excreted in animal milk
Severe impairment (CrCl <30): reduce to 20 mg once daily at bedtime
No specific adjustment defined; use caution in severe impairment
Bladder symptoms, anticholinergic effects, residual urine, IOP in glaucoma risk
summary: Trospium chloride is a quaternary-ammonium antimuscarinic used to treat overactive bladder with urge incontinence, urgency, and frequency. By blocking muscarinic receptors on bladder smooth muscle it reduces detrusor overactivity. Its quaternary structure limits CNS penetration. It must be taken on an empty stomach for adequate absorption and requires dose reduction in severe renal impairment.
indications: Treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency

dosage.n: Take with water on empty stomach, >=1 h before meals

dosage.d: May titrate down to 20 mg once daily based on tolerability

admin: Take with water on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before a meal
Food substantially reduces absorption - do not take with meals
For severe renal impairment, give the once-daily dose at bedtime
moa: Trospium chloride is a muscarinic receptor antagonist. It competitively antagonizes acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in cholinergically innervated organs, including the urinary bladder, reducing detrusor smooth-muscle tone and involuntary contractions. It has negligible nicotinic receptor affinity at therapeutic concentrations, and its quaternary ammonium structure limits central nervous system penetration.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to trospium or ingredients (angioedema, rash, anaphylaxis reported)
relative: Patients at risk for urinary or gastric retention
monitor: Intraocular pressure in patients with glaucoma risk
Anticholinergic CNS effects in the elderly

preg: Limited human data (formerly Pregnancy Category C). Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Trospium is excreted in the milk of lactating animals. A decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking into account its importance to the mother.
renal: In severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min), reduce the dose to 20 mg once daily at bedtime. Trospium is substantially renally eliminated, so accumulation occurs with poor renal function. Not recommended/limited data in end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: No specific dosing recommendation is established; the effect of hepatic impairment has not been adequately studied. Use with caution in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment.

moderate: Drugs eliminated by active renal tubular secretion (e.g., metformin, digoxin, morphine, vancomycin - potential competition)
interactions.food: Food markedly reduces absorption (up to ~70-80%); take on an empty stomach

serious: CNS anticholinergic effects (confusion, hallucinations) in susceptible patients
rare: Heat stroke due to decreased sweating in hot environments

monitoring: Improvement in OAB symptoms (urgency, frequency, incontinence episodes)
Anticholinergic adverse effects, especially in the elderly
Post-void residual / signs of urinary retention
Intraocular pressure in patients with glaucoma risk
counsel: Take on an empty stomach with water, at least 1 hour before meals
May cause dry mouth, constipation, and blurred vision
Use caution with activities requiring alertness until you know how it affects you
Avoid overheating during exercise or hot weather (reduced sweating)
Report inability to urinate, severe eye pain, or facial/throat swelling immediately
pk: Symptom improvement develops over days to weeks of regular dosing
Plasma peak roughly 5-6 hours after an oral dose (fasting)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep dry
pearls: Quaternary ammonium structure limits CNS penetration - may have fewer central anticholinergic effects than tertiary amines
Low oral bioavailability (~10%) and food dramatically reduces it - empty-stomach dosing is essential
Predominantly renal elimination via active tubular secretion - reduce dose in severe renal impairment
Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism, so few hepatic CYP drug interactions
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on an empty stomach. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule - do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause severe anticholinergic effects: tachycardia, mydriasis, urinary retention, agitation, hallucinations, and dry skin/flushing. Management is supportive with ECG monitoring; treat severe symptoms supportively. A cholinesterase inhibitor (e.g., physostigmine) may be considered for life-threatening central anticholinergic toxicity. Trospium is not appreciably dialyzable in clinically meaningful amounts in overdose.
